chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Eul, people meet you and think: oh, they're lovely. Easy to talk to, warm, funny, somehow already on first-name terms with the barista. You read rooms like a professional and adjust in real time. Ten seconds in, people feel comfortable. Ten minutes in, they've told you about their childhood and their ex. What they don't notice is that you're also quietly checking whether they like you. Constantly. You're charming partly because you're working at it, a little, all the time. Which is fine. Just know that it's work, and you're allowed to clock out whenever you like.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're a professional chameleon. You become whatever the person in front of you seems to want, and you're so good at it that you sometimes forget your own colour. I don't mind, whatever you want. You do mind. You mind a lot, three days later, in the shower, rehearsing what you should have said. You call it being flexible. It's actually avoiding conflict with a smile. And eventually the resentment leaks out sideways, in some weird little comment, and everyone's confused about where it came from. Have the opinion at the time. It's cheaper.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you wrap around people like a vine around a fence, and then wonder why you can't leave the fence. Your sabotage is over-adapting. You change your music, your schedule, your whole vibe, and then feel unseen. Well, yes. You hid. You also sometimes stay with people who are just okay, because being alone feels like being left unwatered. You are not a houseplant. You can survive a weekend by yourself, I promise. Try it. And say what you actually want on the first date. It's attractive, it saves months, and the right person will be relieved.
text.friends-and-work: At work you're the glue. Everyone likes you, you smooth over tensions, clients adore you. You also volunteer for things you don't want to do, because saying no feels rude. With friends you're the heart of the group chat, the one who remembers birthdays and sends the voice note at the right moment. But you have that one friend who drains you, and you keep showing up anyway. Why? Because you hate disappointing people more than you hate being tired. Here's the news: your energy is not a public utility. People can't just plug in.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm easygoing. No. You're accommodating, which is a completely different thing. Easygoing people don't keep a mental list of every time they compromised. You also tell yourself you're not that strong. Please. You've bounced back from things that would knock a tree flat. You're tougher than anyone in your life realises, including you. Stop introducing yourself as the delicate one. The delicate one doesn't survive half of what you've survived and then still turn up to brunch with a smile. Honestly, you're the vine growing through concrete. Act like it.
text.the-fix: The fix, by request of Bom, who is hovering. Have one preference a day, out loud. Restaurant, film, the temperature of the room, I don't care which. Say no once a week without giving a reason. Spend one evening alone and enjoy it on purpose, no apologies. In love, ask early what they want, and tell them what you want in the same conversation. You are incredibly adaptable, and that really is a gift. Use it to grow toward the light, not toward whoever happens to be standing closest. Okay, Bom, I said something nice. Happy?

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul. You've said 'I don't mind' eleven times today.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul keeps a secret list of every compromise. I've seen it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You change your whole vibe for every crush. Pick a colour.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: So is that backbone. Use it. Say no once this week.

spring.intro: Spring Eul, Wood ran your birth season and doubled your element, so you're a vine in a garden full of things to climb. You're charming, adaptable and know everyone. People clock you as the friend who's friends with the bartender in ten minutes. The red flag: you're so good at fitting in that nobody knows what you actually think. You agree with whoever's closest. Your opinion on a film changes depending on who you watched it with. In love you become their taste, their music, their friends. The fix: keep one opinion this week that nobody else in the room shares, and say it out loud. Yes, it will feel weird.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You loved that film with one friend and hated it with another. Same film.

summer.intro: Summer Eul, Fire ran things when you were born and Wood feeds Fire, so your energy flows out as charm. You're the flower that blooms for an audience, and honey, you love an audience. People notice your vibe instantly: warm, cute, effortlessly social. What they also notice is how often you check whether everyone's having fun, including whether they're watching you have fun. Your red flag is performing ease. You look relaxed in every photo and exhausted in every taxi home. In love you hide your needs to stay the low-effort option. The fix: stop caring whether you're liked for one whole evening. Sit in a corner. Survive.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You checked if everyone was having fun nine times. Were you, though?

autumn.intro: Autumn Eul, Metal ran your birth season and Metal cuts Wood. So you grew up reading the room like your survival depended on it, and now you're a professional mood detector. Impressive skill. Terrible habit. People see someone sweet and accommodating. Your friends know you'll say you don't mind and then mind enormously. Your red flag is passive resilience: you bend, bend, bend, then quietly leave without explaining. In love that means one day you're just gone, and they genuinely have no idea why. At work you take on extra tasks and seethe. The fix: say 'actually, I mind' once a week. Out loud. To a human.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: 'I don't mind,' says Eul, minding it with every single cell.

winter.intro: Winter Eul, Water ran your season and feeds your Wood, so you're a bulb that keeps its flower hidden until it's sure. You're quietly perceptive and secretly intense. People think you're shy or easygoing. They have no idea you've already formed detailed opinions about everyone at the table. Your red flag is keeping your inner life so private that people misjudge you, and then being hurt that they misjudged you. In love you wait to be discovered instead of letting yourself be known. At work your best ideas stay in your notes app. The fix: share one thought before you've polished it. People can't water what they can't see.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your notes app has better ideas than the whole meeting. Say one, Eul.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Eul. Your vine has plenty of support, which makes you socially fearless and very good at getting your way without anyone noticing. The blind spot: you're a velvet-gloved strategist. Not evil. Just tactical. You know who to charm, when to sulk, how to get the plan changed while everyone thinks it was their idea. It works. It also means people never get a straight answer from you. The fix: next time you want something, ask for it directly. No charm, no hint, no strategy. Just the request. Scary, I know.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Eul, so your vine has little to hold onto and grabs whatever's nearby: people, opinions, plans, a new aesthetic every season. The blind spot: you lose yourself in whoever you're with. With one friend you're sporty, with another you're arty, with your partner you're whatever they like. Everyone thinks they know you. Nobody quite does. The fix: write down five things you like that nobody taught you to like. Keep them when the people around you change. That list is you, and it deserves a spine as much as a trellis.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair colour twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
